Unofficially founded in 1920, officially as [[Football Association Penang|Football Association of Penang]] on 21 October 1921, the club represents the state of Penang in football tournaments.{{cite web |title=Penang Vs Perak Prediction, Head-To-Head, Live Stream Time, Date, Team News, Lineup News, Odds, Stats, Betting Tips Trends, Where To Watch Live Score Malaysian Super League 2023 Telecast Today Match Details – March 31|date=31 March 2023 |url=https://www.sportsunfold.com/penang-vs-perak-prediction-head-to-head-live-stream-time-date-team-news-lineup-news-odds-stats-betting-tips-trends-where-to-watch-live-score-malaysian-super-league-2023-telecast-today-match-d/|publisher=Sportsunfold|access-date=31 March 2023}} The team has traditionally worn a blue home kit. They have a long-standing rivalry with [[Kedah FA|Kedah]]; the two teams from the northern region of Malaysia being engaged in what has been collectively known as the ''"Northern Region Derby"''.{{cite web |title=Late Goal Rescues Kedah Point in Northern Malaysia Derby|date=13 March 2021|url=https://football-tribe.com/asia/2021/03/13/late-goal-rescues-kedah-point-in-northern-malaysia-derby/|publisher=Football Tribe|access-date=13 March 2021}} The club plays their home matches at the 20,000 capacity [[City Stadium (Penang)|City Stadium]] in [[George Town, Penang|George Town]]. Penang had established itself as a major force in Malaysian football between the 1950s to the 1970s.{{cite web |title=Penang relegated to second-tier Malaysia League|url=https://football-tribe.com/asia/2017/09/21/penang-relegated-second-tier-malaysia-league/|publisher=Football Tribe|access-date=17 September 2017}} Domestically, Penang has won a record of 3 [[Malaysia Super League]] titles, 1 [[Malaysia Premier League]] title, 4 [[Malaysia Cup]], 5 [[Malaysia FAM League]] titles, 1 [[Malaysia FA Cup]] title and 1 [[Malaysia Charity Shield]]. At present, it is one of the 12 teams competing in the [[Malaysia Super League|Malaysian Super League]] and the first club from Malaysia to win an Asian title, [[Aga Khan Gold Cup]], which was the early version of [[AFC Champions League]] in 1976.[https://web.archive.org/web/20210625170505/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/agakhan.html Aga Khan Gold Cup]. [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] at [[Wayback Machine]]. On 16 February 2016, [[Mohd Faiz Subri|Faiz Subri]] scored a [[free kick]] in a 4–1 win over [[Sri Pahang F.C.|Pahang FA]] at the [[City Stadium, Penang|City Stadium]] in [[George Town, Penang|George Town]]. Videos of his free kick soon went viral on social media, and he was nominated by the [[Football Association of Malaysia]] for the [[FIFA Puskás Award]] later that year. In 2017, Faiz was awarded the [[FIFA Puskás Award]] for the free kick goal, becoming the first-ever Asian to have won the international award for the best goal of the year. ==History== The club was founded in 1920, and officially as Football Association of Penang (FAP) in 1921. Penang is the oldest football club in Malaysia and one of the oldest clubs in [[Asia]].[https://oddsfactory.co.uk/oldest-football-clubs/ The Oldest Football Clubs In The World – oddsfactory.co.uk][https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=b5KJKlCLXCo&feature=youtu.be 3 Pasukan Bola Sepak Tertua di Malaysia – ML Studios (In Malay)] Penang is the fourth most successful team in Malaysian football history with 16 titles.{{fact|date=August 2024}} ===Early years (1920 – 1950s)=== On 21 October 1921, the club was officially founded. Almost all the big matches were played at Victoria Green, home of the Chinese Recreation Club. They lost its first cup final in 1934 to [[Singapore FA]] with a score of 1–2.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1934|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay34.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=29 February 2012}}{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1941|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay41.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=29 February 2012}} ===Glory days (1950s – 1970s)=== The 1950s saw Penang producing players such as the country's first Olympian, [[Yeap Cheng Eng]], Yeang Kah Chong, Tan Swee Hock, Wong Kam Poh, Yap Hin Hean, Liew Fee Yuen, Lee Ah Loke, and the Pang brothers. Since the early 1950s, [[Aziz Ahmad (football)|Aziz Ahmad]] was Penang's top goal-scorer. He scored the winning goal as Penang defeated Singapore 3–2 in the 1953 Malaya Cup final in [[Ipoh]].{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1953|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay53.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=4 January 2018}} Penang won 3 [[Malaysia Cup]]s (1953, 1954 and 1958) and 4 [[Malaysia FAM League|FAM Cup]] champions (1952, 1955, 1956 and 1957).{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malaycuphist.html|title=Malaysia - List of Cup Winners|access-date=18 March 2021|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}} Some of the well-known FAP officials were Loh Hoot Yeang, who was president for many years, A. S. Mohamad Mydin, Tan Cheng Hoe, Yaakob Syed and Haris Hussain.{{fact|date=August 2024}} David Choong was president in 1962 when Penang made the FAM Cup final, but lost 3–4 to [[Selangor FA|Selangor]] in a contest on May 12 at the City Stadium.{{fact|date=August 2024}} In October 1963, Penang trounced [[Perlis FA|Perlis]] 13–0 in a Malaysia Cup tie.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1963|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay63.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=10 January 2019}} Aziz took over as captain when Cheng Eng retired.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} By 1965, veterans such as Siang Teik and Aziz made way as Penang rebuilt.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} M. Kuppan took over as captain with Yeap Kim Hock, James Raju and Ibrahim Mydin.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} For the first time, Penang preferred the services of four British airmen based at the [[RAF]] support unit at the [[RMAF Butterworth|Butterworth]] base, which participated in the local league. They were John Leather, Clive Warren, Vic Probert and Alan Peacock. The late 1960s saw the emergence of Aziz's nephews, the Abdullah brothers—[[Namat Abdullah|Namat]] and [[Shaharuddin Abdullah|Shaharuddin]]. At his peak, Shaharuddin was a goal-scorer together with [[Isa Bakar]].{{fact|date=August 2024}} Penang made the Malaysia Cup final in 1968 to face mighty Selangor. Selangor romped home 8–1 in one of the most one-sided finals ever {{cite web |title=Malaysia 1968|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay68.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=4 January 2018}} In 1974, Penang heroically knocked Singapore out in the semifinal to face northern rival [[Perak FA|Perak]] in the final. [[Namat Abdullah]] led Penang to a 2–1 victory in what was to be the state's last Malaysia Cup final victory.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1974|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay74.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=29 February 2012}} Penang stepped into the final of Malaysia Cup in 1977 as they lost the match to Singapore.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1977|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay77.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=29 February 2012}} In 1976, Penang became the first and only club from Malaysia to win the [[Aga Khan Gold Cup]] which was the early version of the [[AFC Champions League|Asian Club Championship]], beating [[Mohammedan Sporting Club (Dhaka)|Dhaka Mohammedan Sporting Club]] 3–0 in the final at the [[Bangabandhu National Stadium]] under the guidance of Lim Boon Kheng.{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/sport/football/2016/02/06/former-penang-football-player-boon-kheng-dies-at-76/|title=Former Penang player Boon Kheng dies at 76|work=The Star|accessdate=6 February 2016|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210708121745/https://www.thestar.com.my/sport/football/2016/02/06/former-penang-football-player-boon-kheng-dies-at-76/|archivedate=8 July 2021|url-status=dead}} ===Stagnation (1980s – mid-1990s)=== [[Football Association of Malaysia]] introduced the [[Liga Malaysia (1982–1988)|Malaysia First Division League]] in 1982. Penang was one of the founding members of the league. The first edition saw Penang becoming the champion.{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malaychamp.html|title=Malaysia - List of Champions|access-date=18 March 2021|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}} In 1983, Penang was the first runner-up of the league. After that, the team faced stagnation until the mid-1990s and failed to win any major trophy. ===Resurgence (late 1990s – early 2000s)=== The glory days came after more than 15 years. Penang entered into the FA Cup final in 1997 and lost to Selangor.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1997-FA Cup|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay97.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=19 June 2003}} After the disappointment, Penang won the [[1998 Liga Perdana 1|1998 Malaysia Super League]].{{cite web |title=Malaysia 1998-Premier One|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay98.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=19 June 2003}} The team failed to defend the title as they were the runners-up in 1999. The 2000 FA Cup saw Penang lost to [[Terengganu FA|Terengganu]] after a nail-biting penalties.{{cite web |title=Malaysia First Level-FA Cup 2000 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay00.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=1 April 2001}} Penang was the runner-up of the top division in 2000. After two consecutive years as the runner-up, Penang become the champion in [[2001 Liga Perdana 1|2001]].{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2001-Premier One|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay01.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=3 February 2002}} Penang FA historically won the FA Cup for the first time in 2002.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2002-FA Cup|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay02.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=5 February 2003}} ===Walking downhill and financial crisis (2003 – 2009)=== Although the team got a good start by winning the first [[Piala Sumbangsih|Charity Shield]], they finished mid-table in the league and third in the group stage of the Malaysia Cup.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2003-Charity Shield 2003|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay03.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=17 February 2004}} In 2004, Penang ranked fifth out of 8 in the league and got eliminated in the second round of the FA Cup.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2004|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay04.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=17 February 2004}} The league performance in 2006 was a bit worse as they ranked sixth. Penang won the first round of the FA Cup, but failed to qualify for the third round. The next season saw Penang ranked sixth in the league and lose the first round of the FA Cup. The team lost the quarter-final matches of the Malaysia Cup. In 2006–07 season, the team ranked tenth throughout the league. Penang finished the journey of the FA Cup in round one, as fifth out of six in the group stage. Mohd Bakar was appointed in the 2007–08 season. The Panthers finished 12th in the league, round two in FA Cup and last in the Malaysia Cup group stage. From then until 2012, the club was facing a critical financial condition. In 2009, Penang FA finished third from the last in the top division league.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2009|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay09.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=17 February 2010}} Penang was knocked out from the FA Cup in round two for two consecutive years. Penang was eliminated from the Malaysia Cup tournament after finished third in the group stage. ===Darkest period (2010 – 2012)=== In 2010, the darkest period ever in the team history came. [[Reduan Abdullah]] squad had only collected 10 points and finished at the bottom of the league.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2010-Liga Super 2010|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay2010.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=18 July 2013}} Penang was relegated from the top flight after 18 consecutive spells. The club continued to decline and in 2011 they were relegated further, after the team struggled in the second division with only 4 points in 22 matches.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2011-Liga Premier 2011|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay2011.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=18 July 2013}} [[Janos Krecska]] was appointed as [[head coach]] in 2012. The team finished mid-table in the third tier. ===The comeback (2013 – 2015)=== Penang FA's legend, [[Merzagua Abderrazak]], took over in [[2013 Malaysia FAM League|2013]]. The aim of the promotion was achieved successfully under the new tactician.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2013-FAM Liga 2013|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay2013.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=10 August 2017}} Penang [[2013 Malaysia FAM League|won]] a silverware after an 11-year wait.{{cite web |title=Moroccan Merzagua who guided Penang to promotion not eligible to coach team|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/sport/football/2013/06/04/no-more-merzagua-magic-moroccan-who-guided-penang-to-promotion-not-eligible-to-coach-team/|work=The Star|date=4 June 2013 |access-date=4 June 2013}} The club appointed [[K. Devan]] as the new head coach. Under his guidance Penang claimed the third spot of the Premier League and qualified in the Malaysia Cup after four years. Penang finished last in the group stage with four points after six matches. K. Devan's contract was not renewed and he was signed by [[Negeri Sembilan FA|Negeri Sembilan]]. [[Jacksen F. Tiago]] took over for the next season. Penang stepped into the quarter-final of the Malaysia FA Cup after 13 years. A dramatic finish in the [[2015 Malaysia Premier League|2015]] league campaign saw Penang FA as the runner-up and a ticket to the top flight.{{cite web |title=Malaysia 2015-Liga Premier 2015|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay2015.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=7 Nov 2019}} ===In the top flight (2016 – 2017)=== Penang beefed their squad with several youngsters from the Harimau Muda project and signed three new imports. The Panthers were hopeful of at least staying in the MSL, but found themselves stuck in the relegation zone. The appointment of the MSL winning coach [[Bojan Hodak]] as chief executive officer and [[Nenad Bacina]] as head coach offered some promise for the second half of the season, but Penang still struggled to find consistency. It wasn't until the final day of the season that Penang saved their top flight status, thanks to the goal from [[Faizat Ghazli]].{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-my/news/3896/malaysia/2016/10/25/28808632/local-boy-saves-penang-but-doesnt-want-hero-tag|title=Local boy saves Penang but doesn't want hero tag|access-date=25 October 2016|publisher=Goal.com}} [[I-League]] winning coach [[Ashley Westwood (footballer, born 1976)|Ashley Westwood]] signed a two years contract with the club in November 2016 to replace Nenad and Bojan. However, Penang FA terminated their contract under mutual consent due to poor results in March 2017, and he was replaced by [[Zainal Abidin Hassan]]. Zairil Khir Johari, who took over from Nazir Ariff Mushir Ariff, has resigned as president of the Penang Football Association (FA). Former player [[Reinaldo Lobo]] had reported PFA to [[FIFA]] after the club failed to pay him for six months. ===Relegated to the Malaysia Premier League (2018 – 2020)=== After the relegation, Zainal Abidin Hassan remains the head coach. Players like [[Mohd Faiz Subri]], [[Yong Kuong Yong]], [[Sanna Nyassi]] and [[Mohd Azrul Ahmad]] were retained. The departures saw [[Syamer Kutty Abba]] moving to Johor, [[Jafri Firdaus Chew]] & [[K. Reuben]] to [[PKNS FC]], [[Rafiuddin Rodin]] to Perak. They finished in 10th position and avoided a successive drop. Dr. Amar Pritpal Abdullah was elected as Penang FA president after edging out Datuk Seri Ho Kwee Cheng. Penang FA searched for stability ahead of the 2019 season under the helm of new management. The FA of Penang have set a modest target, to stay in the Premier League. [[Manzoor Azwira]] bought new import player like [[Casagrande]] and [[Ezequiel Agüero|Sergio Aguero]] and Penang FA climbed to the 2nd place, securing the Super League promotion. However, less than 24 hours later, Penang FA found themselves back in the Premier League after being docked six points due to Reinaldo Lobo case. In 2020 the government stopped all sports activities due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Penang FA was on track of winning the league after being unbeaten in 8 matches. They secure promotion to the Super League after beating [[Kuala Lumpur FA|Kuala Lumpur]] 2–1 at City Stadium.{{cite web|url=https://football-tribe.com/malaysia/2020/09/22/penang-promoted-to-super-league-2021/|title=Penang promoted to Super League 2021|date=22 September 2020|access-date=22 September 2020|publisher=Football Tribe}} Penang celebrated their first ever MPL title after beating [[Kelantan United F.C.|Kelantan United]] 4-0 and got promoted to the [[2021 Malaysia Super League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nst.com.my/sports/football/2020/10/629462/rampant-penang-clinch-pl-title|title=Rampant Penang clinch PL title|date=4 October 2020|access-date=4 October 2020|publisher=New Straits Times}} ===Privatisation (2020)=== On 21 September 2020, Penang FA was officially privatised and rebranded as Penang Football Club.{{cite web |title=Top six target for Penang FC|date=4 March 2021 |url=https://www.buletinmutiara.com/top-six-target-for-penang-fc/|publisher=Buletin Mutiara |access-date=4 March 2021}} Subsequently, Penang FC Sdn. Bhd. was established as a subsidiary of the [[Penang state government]] under Chief Minister Incorporated (CMI), a state government agency.{{cite web |title=Top six target for Penang FC|date=4 March 2021 |url=https://www.buletinmutiara.com/top-six-target-for-penang-fc/|publisher=Buletin Mutiara |access-date=4 March 2021}} This privatisation step is part of the [[Football Association of Malaysia]] (FAM) efforts to comply with FIFA's directive, which requires a separation between football governing bodies and professional clubs.{{cite web |title=New name for Penang football team|date=15 October 2020 |url=https://www.buletinmutiara.com/new-name-for-penang-football-team/|publisher=Buletin Mutiara |access-date=6 March 2021}} The rebranding also includes a new logo and visual identity to reflect the modern era of football in Penang. The [[Football Association Penang|Football Association of Penang]] (FAP) remains the governing body responsible for grassroots development, while Penang FC Sdn. Bhd. operates as a corporate entity managing the state’s professional football team.{{cite web|url=https://www.buletinmutiara.com/fap-building-talent-for-long-term-success/|title=FAP building talent for long-term success|date=February 2023 |publisher=Buletin Mutiara}} ===Return to the top flight (2021–present)=== Penang FC achieved third place in the [[2021 Malaysia Super League]], marking a significant milestone in the club's history since the inaugural [[2004 Malaysia Super League]] season. It was their first season in the top tier of Malaysian football following their promotion in [[2020 Malaysia Premier League|2020]]. Although the club performed well in the cup by reaching the [[2022 Malaysia FA Cup]] semi-final, Penang FC struggled in the league, finishing 12th—the last place—in the [[2022 Malaysia Super League]], a position that would normally mean relegation to the [[Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]. The first had background colours of the club crest, navy blue and white. At the top left and bottom right of the crest are the capital letters of 'F' and 'A', which are the abbreviation of 'Football Association'. At the bottom left is a leather ball. The [[Prince of Wales's feathers]] and its motto, 'Ich Dien' which means 'I serve' were at top left of the crest. The name of the state, 'Penang', is written in capital letters. In the early 1990s, the crest underwent some variations as part of an attempt to modernise the previous crest. The capital letters of 'F' and 'A' were changed into three-dimensional form, with navy blue edges and white fill colour. The ball at the bottom left was changed into a modern ball with pentagonal and hexagonal patterns, and the Prince of Wales's feathers on the top left were also modernised, colours for both elements were changed. Penang's traditional home colours are sky blue and yellow which are taken from the colours of the Penang state flag. Navy blue and yellow have also been used severally. Traditional away kit colours have been either yellow or white. ==Supporters== Penang's traditional fanbase comes from all over the George Town area including the other suburbs such as [[Jelutong]], [[Air Itam]], [[Tanjung Bungah]], [[Bayan Lepas]] and even from the mainland. Penang's hardcore supporters are the so-called Ultras Panthers supporters, also known as Green Terrace Comrades UP11. Ultras Panthers was founded in 2011. In every match the Penang team played, they will be found in a group standing at the supporters area. The main colours for these supporters are usually in blue with a blue-yellow scarf and banners just like the Penang's team kits colours. These supporters always bring drums and large colorful flags to the stadiums. Established in 2017, the Penang Football Fans Club (PFFC) is the official supporter club which is registered under the law of Malaysia.[https://penangfootballfans.wixsite.com/pffc Penang Football Fans Club official website] The main mission of PFFC is to unite football supporters in Penang. Besides it will also act as a channel between the fans and the team. There are also numerous supporters clubs such as Demi Pulau Pinang, Penang Brotherhood, Penang FC Fan Club, Haria Penang 69, Nindia Bandaraya, Brigade 07, Boys Of North and more in the state.[https://m.facebook.com/PenangBrotherhood/ Penang Brotherhood Facebook] Penang had an average gate of 7,301 in the 2016 competitive campaign. Sometimes, tourists from foreign countries also attended the matches. As of June 2020, Penang had 134,650 followers on social media, the ninth highest among football clubs in Malaysia. At matches, Penang fanatic fans sing chants such as "Haria Penang Haria",[https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=1QNzXYnnJcI Haria Penang Haria On YouTube] "Sehati Sejiwa" which means "One Heart, One Soul" and the state anthem "Untuk Negeri Kita", which means "For our state", to boost their beloved players' morale. Fans also throw toilet rolls to the pitch before the match begins. The well-known and popular slogan among Penang FC supporters is "Haria Penang Haria". It is used as "words of spirit" during and off the game, and as the slogan among supporters. ==Rivalries== [[Kedah Darul Aman F.C.|Kedah Darul Aman]] is the biggest rival for Penang. Penang fans consider their main rivalries to be with (in order) Kedah, [[Perak F.C.|Perak]] and [[Perlis F.A.|Perlis]]. Matches against fellow northern region sides [[Perlis United F.C.|Perlis United]], [[Kuala Muda Naza F.C.|Kuala Muda Naza]], [[Kedah United F.C.|Kedah United]], [[Sungai Ara F.C.|Sungai Ara]], [[PBAPP F.C.|PBAPP]], [[SDMS Kepala Batas F.C.|SDMS Kepala Batas]], Bukit Tambun, and [[Perak YBU F.C.|Perak YBU]] have only taken place intermittently, due to the clubs often being in separate divisions. ===Derby=== Northern Region Derby is the name given to football matches that involves Penang and Kedah.{{cite web |last1=Tacts |first1=Axello |title=Menanti Tiupan Wisel Permulaan Derbi Utara Malam Ini, Pulau Pinang vs Kedah!|work=SEMUANYA BOLA |date=21 July 2017|url=https://www.semuanyabola.com/derbi-utara-pulau-pinang-kedah/|language=ms|access-date=22 July 2017}} Both of them were located in the northern region of Malaysia. [[City Stadium (Penang)|City Stadium]] or [[Penang State Stadium]] and [[Darul Aman Stadium]] are packed by fans from Kedah and Penang during derby matches. The match usually creates a lively atmosphere, with numerous banners unfolded before the start of the game. ===Friendships=== Although Penang's main rivals mostly are from the northern region of Malaysia, especially Kedah, but there is also a strong supporter of friendship with Kedah and there are good relations with the fans of [[Perak F.C.|Perak]] and [[Perlis FA|Perlis]]. Penang Football Club (simply known as Penang FC) is a Malaysian professional football club based in George Town, Penang, that competes in Malaysia Super League, the top tier of Malaysian football.
Unofficially founded in 1920, officially as Football Association of Penang on 21 October 1921, the club represents the state of Penang in football tournaments. The team has traditionally worn a blue home kit.
They have a long-standing rivalry with Kedah; the two teams from the northern region of Malaysia being engaged in what has been collectively known as the "Northern Region Derby". The club plays their home matches at the 20,000 capacity City Stadium in George Town.
Penang had established itself as a major force in Malaysian football between the 1950s to the 1970s. Domestically, Penang has won a record of 3 Malaysia Super League titles, 1 Malaysia Premier League title, 4 Malaysia Cup, 5 Malaysia FAM League titles, 1 Malaysia FA Cup title and 1 Malaysia Charity Shield. At present, it is one of the 12 teams competing in the Malaysian Super League and the first club from Malaysia to win an Asian title,  Aga Khan Gold Cup, which was the early version of AFC Champions League in 1976.
On 16 February 2016, Faiz Subri scored a free kick in a 4–1 win over Pahang FA at the City Stadium in George Town. Videos of his free kick soon went viral on social media, and he was nominated by the Football Association of Malaysia for the FIFA Puskás Award later that year. In 2017, Faiz was awarded the FIFA Puskás Award for the free kick goal, becoming the first-ever Asian to have won the international award for the best goal of the year.
